title: What auditors and the grand jury found about overruns and change orders
question: What have the City's own reviewers put in writing about change orders, cost overruns and late projects?
finding: 14 findings from 10 reports, 2014 to 2026. The most recent: Approved change orders added $186.8 million (8%) to 297 construction contracts at five departments, July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024; by department the increase ran from 3 percent to 33 percent of the first contract value. Departments that build public works make little use of the contract terms meant to protect the City against delay, cost overruns and poor work by contractors. The contractor evaluation database was still not in use; departments lacked the leadership, guidelines, procedures and training to use it. The reviewers describe weak records and weak enforcement inside departments, and a contractor evaluation database that the law requires and departments do not use; none of the reports on disk ranks contractors by change orders.
how: The official documents on disk (Controller audits, Budget and Legislative Analyst performance audits, Civil Grand Jury reports) were searched for change orders, cost overruns and schedule. Each row gives a sentence that restates a passage, written only when the figures it uses are found in the text on disk, and a quote of at most twelve words lifted from that text by the script.
limits: A finding by an auditor or a grand jury is that body's conclusion at the time; departments answered each report and several findings may since have been acted on. The reports sample contracts and years. The quotes are short and each row links to the full document for context.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: Approved change orders added $186.8 million (8%) to 297 construction contracts at five departments, July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024; by department the increase ran from 3 percent to 33 percent of the first contract value.
rows.quote: “ranged from 3 percent to 33 percent across departments”

document.t: Performance Audit of the Procurement of Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6 of the Administrative Code by Public Works, the Airport, the Port, Recreation and Parks, and Municipal Transportation Agency

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: Departments that build public works make little use of the contract terms meant to protect the City against delay, cost overruns and poor work by contractors.
rows.quote: “underutilizing protective mechanisms included in public works contracts”

document.t: Performance Audit of the Procurement of Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6 of the Administrative Code by Public Works, the Airport, the Port, Recreation and Parks, and Municipal Transportation Agency

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: The contractor evaluation database was still not in use; departments lacked the leadership, guidelines, procedures and training to use it.
rows.quote: “Required Contractor Evaluation Database is Still Not in Use”

document.t: Performance Audit of the Procurement of Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6 of the Administrative Code by Public Works, the Airport, the Port, Recreation and Parks, and Municipal Transportation Agency

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: At the Public Utilities Commission, 54 of 91 construction contracts (July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2022) had at least one change order, and fourteen of those 54 (26 percent) grew by more than 10 percent through change orders.
rows.quote: “had their project budgets increased by more than 10 percent”

document.t: Performance Audit of the Authority Delegated to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission for Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: The Public Utilities Commission keeps no central record of change-order documents for projects with budgets under $10 million, which its own policy requires.
rows.quote: “no central database or other record-keeping system for construction change order documentation”

document.t: Performance Audit of the Authority Delegated to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission for Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: None of the departments that build public works consistently recorded how its construction contractors performed in the database the Administrative Code requires for that: as of August 2024 only 12 of the 176 projects entered in it had a completed evaluation.
rows.quote: “are not using the City’s contractor performance and evaluation database”

document.t: Performance Audit of the Authority Delegated to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission for Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6

rows.said: Two buildings paid for by the 2014 earthquake-safety bond finished above plan, by more than their contingency: the police Traffic Company and Forensic Services building ($165 million planned, $178.9 million final) and the Chief Medical Examiner building ($65 million planned, $67.5 million final).
rows.quote: “their cost overruns exceeded their contingency budget”

document.t: Building San Francisco: Designing, Constructing, and Maintaining City Infrastructure

rows.said: The renovation of the City-owned Portsmouth Square garage ran $4.5 million (52 percent) over, and more than $1 million of planned work was cut to cover it.
rows.quote: “resulted in a $4.5 million (52 percent) cost overrun”

document.t: The PPPC Board Was Not Equipped to Effectively Manage the Portsmouth Garage Renovation Project and Rec & Park, as the Project Owner, Did Not Adequately Monitor the Project

rows.said: On the Van Ness Avenue project, when poorly documented utility lines were found, the contract gave the builder a reason to stop and seek paid modifications for the unplanned work.
rows.quote: “the contractor’s incentive was to pause work while it pursued contract modifications”

document.t: Van Ness Avenue: What Lies Beneath

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: The Office of Contract Administration, which reviews Public Works construction change orders, had no written guidelines for that review and had not set out grounds for refusing a change.
rows.quote: “has not developed written guidelines governing the review”

document.t: Street Resurfacing Program and StreetTreeSF Program Performance Audit

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor
rows.said: Poor communication between the transit agency's construction, transit and finance divisions contributed to delays of up to 1.7 years and cost overruns of up to $9 million on four projects the Controller examined.
rows.quote: “cost overruns of up to $9 million for four projects”

document.t: SFMTA Needs to Improve Accountability and Collaboration in Its Capital Planning and Project Delivery Processes

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: The two bus-line projects the auditors followed to the end of 2018, the 14 Mission and the 22 Fillmore, were unfinished, behind schedule and over budget.
rows.quote: “not yet completed, behind schedule, over budget”

document.t: Performance Audit of San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency’s (SFMTA) Revenues, Ridership, and Congestion Management

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor
rows.said: On the Public Utilities Commission's Crystal Springs/San Andreas pipeline contract the price went from $99,763,000 to $132,421,418 after modifications and change orders, a 33 percent increase; the Commission fully followed 22 of 26 close-out procedures.
rows.quote: “the final contract amount was $132,421,418, a 33 percent increase”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor
rows.said: City departments do not adequately assess how construction contractors perform, and past performance is not considered when City construction contracts are awarded.
rows.quote: “do not consider past performance in the construction contract award process”

document.t: Citywide construction: contractor performance evaluation audit
